title: Cut a Twisted Paper Loop in Half: You Get ONE Ring #math #mobiusstrip
description:
Take a strip of paper, give it one half twist, and tape the ends into a loop. That is a Möbius strip: it has only one side and one edge. Now cut it lengthwise down the middle. You would expect two rings. You get one ring, twice as long. Follow one half of the strip: the half twist joins it to the other half, so the two halves were always one strip that goes round twice. The new ring is twisted (two full twists) and is no longer a Möbius strip. Cut a third of the way in from the edge instead and you get two rings, linked: a thin Möbius strip and a longer ring twice its length. Try it with paper, tape and scissors.
